conventions.convention: Plane curves are reduced zero sets of nonconstant square-free homogeneous forms over an algebraically closed field; every component occurs once.

Local intersection multiplicity is the ambient local-ring quotient length; it is zero off the intersection and infinite when a common local component passes through the point. Local components here are algebraic local-ring factors, distinguished from formal branches in the node example.
The tangent cone uses the lowest nonzero homogeneous part; tangent lines are its linear factors with their exponents.
The eliminating resultant retains nominated degrees d and e even after specialization. Finite-root detection requires the elimination centre [0:0:1] to lie on neither curve.
Bézout assumes Choice, algebraic closure, positive degrees and no common component, and counts local lengths rather than distinct points.
Flexes are smooth points with finite tangent-line contact at least three; tangent lines that are components are excluded. Bitangents use two distinct points of contact multiplicity at least two.
Lie(G) is the tangent space at the rational identity, equivalently the dual-number reduction kernel. R[ε] means ε²=0; exponential notation denotes this correspondence, not an analytic exponential.
The bracket is [X,Y]=Lie(Ad)(X)Y and the matrix commutator is XY−YX; alternation is proved also in characteristic two.
The locally-free-differentials smoothness equivalence requires characteristic zero, local finite type and Choice; free differentials alone do not imply smoothness in characteristic p.
Simple rational modules are nonzero; semisimple means an internal direct sum of simple submodules, including the empty sum for zero. Rational representations may be infinite-dimensional.

Positive roots are those of B. Dominance uses nonnegative simple-coroot pairings; λ≥μ means λ−μ is a nonnegative integral combination of simple roots. Fundamental weights lie in the rational root span and need not be torus characters.
Primitive vectors span B-stable lines; equivalently, under the stated structural Choice premise, they are fixed by the positive unipotent radical U and are T-eigenvectors.
E(λ) uses the opposite Borel B⁻, right covariance f(gb)=f(g)λ(b⁻¹), and left action (gf)(x)=f(g⁻¹x). Its primitive fixed line is E(λ)^U.

Central-isogeny highest-weight identification uses compatible source and target Borel pairs. The reductive product cover uses the largest central torus Z(G)_t, not a possibly nonreduced neutral component.

load_bearing.statement: For every commutative k-algebra R, the dual-number reduction kernel is naturally the R-module Lie(G)⊗kR, with multiplication equal to addition. Lie is functorial on finite-type group schemes and injective on closed immersions; the proof is choice-free.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every affine group scheme of finite type over a characteristic-zero field is smooth; every local ring is regular and the group is reduced.

Assume inherited Choice. A rational module of a split reductive group generated by a primitive vector v of weight λ is generated by v under U⁻, has top weight space kv and all other weights strictly below λ, has dominant λ, and has a largest proper submodule with simple quotient.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Plane projective curves of positive degrees d,e over an algebraically closed field, with no common component, satisfy the finite identity Σp∈C∩D I_p(C,D)=de.

Assume inherited Choice. For split semisimple G, Z(G)=∩α ker α and X(Z(G))=X(T)/ZΦ; a simple module of highest weight λ has central character λ+ZΦ. For a central isogeny of split reductive groups, a simple source module descends exactly when its highest weight belongs to the target character lattice; it remains simple and has that highest weight for compatible Borel pairs.

Assume inherited Choice. Every closed subgroup scheme H of an affine finite-type group scheme G over a field is the scheme-theoretic stabilizer of a line in a finite-dimensional rational G-representation; for L=kv, Lie(H)={x:xv∈kv}.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. If A is a finite-type algebra over a characteristic-zero field and Ω_A/k localized at a prime q is free over A_q, then A_q is regular.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. At a common point of plane projective curves over an algebraically closed field with no common local component, I_p(C,D)≥m_p(C)m_p(D), with equality exactly when the tangent cones share no line.

Assume inherited Choice. For a finite-dimensional rational representation of a characteristic-zero semisimple group with nonzero derived Lie image, that image is semisimple, its faithful trace form is nondegenerate, and its Casimir acts as a G-module endomorphism of trace equal to the image's dimension.
Assume inherited Choice. Every dominant torus character of a split semisimple group over k occurs as a primitive weight of a rational representation; consequently E(λ)≠0.

Assume inherited Choice. For a split reductive group over any field and a chosen Borel pair, highest weight gives a bijection between simple rational-module isomorphism classes and dominant torus characters. Each simple has a one-dimensional highest weight space and all remaining weights strictly below it.

concerns.concern: The Statement says weight spaces have 'the same dimension', and Proof 2.1 writes dim_k V_λ=dim_k V_wλ, although V is an arbitrary rational representation. The opened def-dimension defines numerical dimension only for finite-dimensional spaces and explicitly assigns no number in the infinite-dimensional case. The proof already establishes the correctly typed isomorphism using a k-valued normalizer representative; clarify the dimension clause for finite-dimensional weight spaces or supply a cardinal-dimension convention. This does not undermine the isomorphism or Weyl stability.

seams_checked.note: Matrix-group point formulas, GL₀, and faithful closed embeddings are used with their actual finite-type hypotheses. The inherited Choice premise for finite-type assertions and bracket uniqueness is retained.

The comodule dictionary permits arbitrary vector spaces, while finite-subcomodule arguments justify finite simples and singly generated modules. Chevalley uses scheme-theoretic Hopf ideals and all algebra-valued points; faithful embedding and finite-generation uses retain Choice.

Uses retain splitness, arbitrary characteristic, structural Choice, smooth standard parabolics, rational Weyl representatives, and dense opposite big cells. The reductive cover uses Z(G)_t and the largest derived-intersection subtorus. Central-isogeny descent explicitly supplies compatible Borel pairs.

This is a page prerequisite/context edge. The opened Chow page and the reference/dependency scan of its listed A-page items contain no direct citation or restatement of an owned plane-curve item, so no strengthened Bézout interface was found.

The split-reductive and root Definitions use the affine adjoint representation in its stated domain. The Lie-functor lemma faithfully uses the general finite-type tangent-kernel identification and proves its limit, centralizer and normalizer extensions locally; it identifies agreement with the affine adjoint supplier only for affine G.
